list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden until earned. Names, descriptions and grades as published by PlayStation, as listed by PSNProfiles and cross-checked on Exophase; progress targets as published by PSNProfiles. All guides in this file are the Leonida Ledger's own words. Retrieved 2026-11-19.

trophies.guide: The platinum is the receipt for the other 54 trophies: no separate task, no extra mission, no shortcut. Finish the story, clear the side strands, grind the counters and sweep up the cryptic five, and this pops the moment the last one lands. Treat the 7-stage roadmap as the order of work and this trophy takes care of itself.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list: the official name, description and grade. Retrieved 2026-11-19.
Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5): cross-check of the official name, description and grade. Retrieved 2026-11-19.
Leonida Ledger — own reading: the steps above are our reading of the official description, not yet checked in play.
steps: Work the roadmap stage by stage, story first.
Clear every counter trophy before the final cleanup.
Check the tracker: when 54 of 55 show earned, one trophy is left.
Earn that last trophy and the platinum pops with it.
trophies.where: Everywhere — it is earned by earning the other 54 trophies.

trophies.guide: 100% completion — the gold that makes the platinum hard. The official description gives no checklist, and Rockstar has not spelled out what the 100% covers, so treat the visible counters as the workload: story, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the rest of the list. This is a last-stage trophy: chase it only when everything else is nearly done, and let the tracker tell you what is left.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: 250 stunts. A stunt is any showy driving moment the game counts — jumps, near misses, long drifts and air time all feed the same counter, so drive fast and loose and the number climbs on its own. This is a background grind: do not hunt it early, let it build while you play, and finish it in free roam once the story is done.

trophies.where: The open roads of Leonida, in free roam. PSN tracks it 0/250.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. The description does not name the nine, so treat it as a sampler: fishing, racing, the shooting range, the arcade, bowling, drone racing and the rest of the activities the game offers. One try each is enough — no wins needed, no medals needed. Tick them off as you find them and the trophy pops on the ninth type.

Work through the ranges one challenge at a time, learn each one's rhythm, and save the hardest golds for a focused session rather than forcing them mid-story.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every one of the 18 spots across Leonida. This is the one trophy in the list reported as possibly missable: the first meditation spot is offered in Chapter 1, and the worry — flagged by PowerPyx and echoed across the guide sites — is that a spot offered early may not come back later. Our advice, as an inference from that flag: meditate at every spot the moment it is offered, keep a manual save before Chapter 1's big beats, and never rely on a later replay to catch a missed spot. If you are already past Chapter 1, meditate at every spot you find from here on and keep a save before each new chapter.
trophies.missable_note: Possibly missable — INFERENCE, not confirmed: PowerPyx (via GTA Zone) flags this as the only trophy reported as possibly missable. The first meditation spot is offered in Chapter 1. Meditate at every spot when offered and keep manual saves; no guide has yet confirmed whether a missed spot can be revisited.

Play the way you want, make choices as they come, and the counter fills over a long campaign; treat the profile warning as the one thing to respect.
